name: How to Safely Clean Up After a Small Garage Fire

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Dealing with the aftermath of even a small garage fire can feel daunting, but if it's truly minor and safe, there are some steps you can take. First and foremost, safety is key – make sure the fire is completely extinguished and the area is stable before you even think about cleaning. Wear protective gear: gloves, a N95 mask, and eye protection are a must to protect against soot and fumes. You'll want to open all doors and windows to ventilate the space as much as possible; this helps dissipate smoke and odors. For loose, dry soot, a HEPA-filtered vacuum can be helpful. For hard surfaces, use a mild, non-abrasive cleaner designed for smoke residue, testing it in an inconspicuous area first. Be gentle; scrubbing can embed soot further. For soft items or porous surfaces like drywall, professional help is usually needed, as smoke penetrates deeply. If you're dealing with more than a very small, contained fire, or if smoke odor persists, it's really best to call in the pros. Companies like First To Respond Restoration specialize in this kind of cleanup and have the right tools and expertise to make sure your garage is truly clean and safe again.
